text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Profit-taking helped pull German debt off its session highs in late trading but failed to wipe out all the gains made in Tuesday's unexpected surge higher, aided in part by weak German economic data. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.63, up 0.16 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - December gilt futures closed slightly lower on the day on overseas profit-taking after soaring to a new contract high on Tuesday. Gilts surged in early trade with rising European bond markets, but the upswing was quickly reversed when U.S. markets opened. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-29/32, down 3/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The 10-year bond future ended sharply higher in heavy volume, powered by a U.S. dollar which drew strength from comments by Bundesbank council member Otmar Issing predicting a possible switch to U.S. assets at the start of European monetary union. The December bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.84 up 0.42 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to firmer levels in late afternoon trading supported by the strong lira and rising hopes that the Bank of Italy may cut its key discount rate later this month. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.72 up 0.57 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened higher on Tuesday, bolstered by a strong dollar. The dollar surged to a 23-month high against the mark in London overnight. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 116-14/32, up 18/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.32 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended lower in Tokyo trading on Tuesday. The March contract closed down 0.10 at 126.18, after moving between 126.10 and 126.55. The volume was 44,811 contracts. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.20, down 0.28 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary market enjoyed a significantly more active day on Tuesday, with a number of dollar deals launched, driven by the large amount of dollar redemptions due. "In the past three months, there has been $6.6 billion dollars worth of redemptions of sovereign FRNs, and there has only been $2.0 billion of issuance," a syndicate manager at one of the joint lead managers for the CADES issue said.
